grammar.title: Present perfect para duração: for / since
grammar.explanation_pt:
Este é o uso do present perfect que mais confunde brasileiros. Em português dizemos:
"**Moro** aqui **há** 5 anos" (presente).

Em inglês, se a situação **começou no passado e continua agora**, usamos o **present perfect**:
"I**'ve lived** here **for** 5 years." ✅
"I live here for 5 years." ❌ (erro muito comum!)

**For** + **período** (quanto tempo): for two hours, for three weeks, for ten years, for ages, for a long time.
**Since** + **ponto de partida** (desde quando): since 2019, since Monday, since January, since I was a child, since 8 a.m.

**Pergunta:** **How long have you** + particípio? → "How long have you worked here?"

**Negativa com for/since:** "I **haven't seen** her **for** months." / "We **haven't talked since** the party."

**Stative verbs** (know, be, have, like) usam present perfect simples: "I've **known** him for years." / "She's **been** a teacher since 2010."

examples.en: How long have you had your car? — I've had it for three years.
examples.pt: Há quanto tempo você tem seu carro? — Tenho há três anos.

examples.en: She's been my best friend since we were six.

examples.en: I haven't been to the beach for ages!
examples.pt: Não vou à praia há séculos!

grammar.tip_pt: Compare: "I **lived** in Rio **for** 5 years" (simple past = já não moro mais lá) x "I**'ve lived** in Rio **for** 5 years" (present perfect = ainda moro). Uma palavra muda toda a história!

common_mistakes.right: I've worked here for three years.
common_mistakes.why_pt: Período = for; ponto de partida = since.

pronunciation.focus: For e since fracos e o 've
pronunciation.tip_pt: **For** é fraco: "fâr" ("I've lived here fâr five years"). Não esqueça o **'ve**: "I've lived" ("áivlivd") — sem ele, a frase vira presente ("I lived" / "I live") e muda o sentido.

reading.title: The longest-serving...
reading.text: Some people stay in the same place for an incredibly long time. In Japan, a hotel called Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan has welcomed guests since the year 705 — it's been run by the same family for more than fifty generations. In the UK, a man named Bob Tanner delivered newspapers for 70 years in the same town. And in Brazil, many small businesses have passed from parents to children for decades. Why do people stay? Researchers say a sense of belonging is one of the main reasons: when you've known your neighbors for years and your customers since they were children, leaving feels like losing part of your identity. In a world where people change jobs every few years, these stories feel almost magical.

grammar.title: Already, yet, just (+ still)
grammar.explanation_pt:
Esses três advérbios são os "melhores amigos" do present perfect para falar de ações **recentes** e **tarefas**:

**Already** = já (antes do esperado) → **afirmativas**, entre have e o particípio:
"I**'ve already** paid the bill."

**Yet** → no **fim da frase**:
- **negativas** = ainda (não): "I haven't paid **yet**."
- **perguntas** = já: "Have you paid **yet**?"

**Just** = acabou de (muito recente) → entre have e o particípio:
"She**'s just** arrived." (Ela acabou de chegar.)

**Still** = ainda (com ênfase na demora/frustração) → **antes** do haven't: "I **still haven't** received my package!"

💡 No inglês americano informal, é comum usar o **simple past** com already, yet e just: "Did you eat **yet**?" / "I **just** saw him." Ambos estão certos — mas o present perfect é o padrão em provas e no inglês britânico.

examples.en: Have you booked the flights yet? — Yes, I've already booked them.
examples.pt: Você já reservou os voos? — Sim, já reservei.

examples.en: Sorry, the manager has just left. Can I take a message?

examples.en: It's been three weeks and I still haven't received my refund.

grammar.tip_pt: Cuidado com **"já"**: em perguntas, use **yet** ("Have you finished **yet**?"). **Already** em perguntas mostra **surpresa**: "Have you finished **already**?! That was fast!"

common_mistakes.why_pt: Just vem entre have e o particípio.

pronunciation.tip_pt: **Yet** começa com som de "i" ("iét") — não confunda com **jet** ("djét", jato). **Just** começa com "dj" ("djâst") e o T final é leve: "I've jus(t) arrived".

reading.title: The Zeigarnik effect
reading.text: Have you ever noticed that unfinished tasks stay in your head, while finished ones disappear? This is called the Zeigarnik effect, after a psychologist who observed that waiters remembered unpaid orders perfectly — but forgot them as soon as the customers had paid. Our brains keep "open" tasks active, which can cause stress. Productivity experts suggest a simple solution: write everything down. Once a task is on a list, your brain can relax a little. At the end of the day, look at what you've already done, not only at what you haven't done yet. Celebrating small wins — "I've just answered all my emails!" — keeps you motivated.

questions.answer: Unfinished tasks stay in our heads, while finished ones disappear.

questions.q: What did the waiters remember?
questions.answer: Unpaid orders (and forgot them after customers paid).

grammar.title: Present perfect x simple past
grammar.explanation_pt:
**A pergunta-chave:** o tempo está **terminado** ou **ainda aberto**?

**Simple past** → tempo **terminado e definido**. Você sabe (ou diz) **quando**.
- Palavras: yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago, when I was a child, on Monday, What time...? When...?
- "I **visited** Rome **in 2019**." / "**When did** you **arrive**?"

**Present perfect** → tempo **aberto** ou **não mencionado**; o foco é o **resultado agora** ou a **experiência**.
- Palavras: ever, never, before, already, yet, just, so far, recently, lately, for, since, How long...?
- "I**'ve visited** Rome **three times**." / "**Have** you **ever been** to Rome?"

**Períodos ainda abertos** (today, this week, this month, this year) usam **present perfect** se o período não acabou:
- "I**'ve had** three coffees **today**." (o dia não acabou)
- "I **had** three coffees **yesterday**." (acabou)

**Notícias:** a primeira frase anuncia com present perfect; os detalhes vêm no simple past:
"Scientists **have discovered** a new planet. They **found** it last month using a new telescope."

rows: I saw that movie last week.
She lived in Tokyo for 2 years. (não mora mais)
She's lived in Tokyo for 2 years. (ainda mora)
Did you finish the report yesterday?
Have you finished the report yet?
I wrote three emails this morning. (já é tarde)
I've written three emails this morning. (ainda é manhã)
How long have you known him?

examples.en: We've had a great year so far. Sales grew 20% in the first quarter.
examples.pt: Tivemos um ótimo ano até agora. As vendas cresceram 20% no primeiro trimestre.

grammar.tip_pt: Atalho mental: se dá para responder **"When?"** com uma data ou momento, é **simple past**. Se a resposta é **"Not important"** ou **"Until now"**, é **present perfect**.

common_mistakes.wrong: I've bought this phone two years ago.

common_mistakes.why_pt: Ago indica tempo definido → simple past.
When pede um momento definido → simple past.
Experiência de vida, sem tempo definido → present perfect (padrão).

pronunciation.tip_pt: Na fala rápida, "I've seen" e "I saw" soam bem diferentes, mas "I've finished" e "I finished" podem ser quase iguais — o 've é só um "v" leve. Preste atenção ao **contexto** (palavras como yet, already, yesterday) para entender o tempo.

reading.title: My first year abroad
reading.text: It's been exactly one year since I moved to Montreal, and what a year it's been! When I arrived last September, I didn't speak any French, and my English was basic. I lived in a tiny room and worked in a restaurant kitchen. Since then, a lot has changed. I've taken two French courses, and I've made friends from more than ten countries. I've also found a job in my area — I started as a junior architect in March. Of course, it hasn't all been easy. I've missed my family terribly, and I'll never forget my first winter: in January, the temperature fell to minus 30 degrees, and I cried on my way to work. But so far, moving here has been the best decision of my life.

writing.model:
LOCAL TEACHER WINS NATIONAL AWARD

A public school teacher from Fortaleza has won Brazil's Teacher of the Year award. Marta Lima, 41, received the prize in a ceremony in Brasília last Friday. She created a robotics club with recycled materials in 2021, and her students won three national competitions. "I've taught for eighteen years, and this is the proudest moment of my career," she said. Since the announcement, Marta has received hundreds of messages from former students. The school has already announced that it will open two more robotics clubs next year.

culture_note.title: Manchetes em inglês
culture_note.text_pt: Manchetes de jornal usam um "inglês telegráfico": **presente simples para o passado** ("Teacher **wins** award"), sem artigos e sem verbo to be ("Mayor **to visit** school" = o prefeito vai visitar). Mas o primeiro parágrafo da notícia segue a regra: present perfect + simple past.

summary_pt: Tempo aberto ou não mencionado → present perfect.
ago, last, yesterday, when, in 2020 → simple past.
ever, never, yet, already, just, so far, since → present perfect.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Estrutura:** **have / has been** + verbo**-ing**
- I**'ve been working** here since 2020.
- She**'s been studying** all day.
- **How long have** you **been learning** English?

**Usos:**
1. **Atividade que começou no passado e continua** (ênfase na **duração**/continuidade): "I**'ve been studying** English **for** three years."
2. **Atividade recente com resultado visível agora:** "Why are you so tired?" "I**'ve been running**." / "Your eyes are red. **Have** you **been crying**?"
3. **Atividades temporárias recentes:** "**Lately**, I**'ve been working** from home."

**Simple x continuous:**
- **Continuous** = foco na **atividade/duração**: "I**'ve been writing** emails all morning." (o processo)
- **Simple** = foco no **resultado/quantidade**: "I**'ve written** 20 emails." (quantos — completo)

Com **stative verbs** (know, be, have, like, want), use sempre o **simple**: "I**'ve known** her for years" (❌ "I've been knowing").

Com **work, live, study, teach**, os dois funcionam com for/since: "I've worked / I've been working here for 5 years."

rows: I've been reading this book all week.
We've been saving money for a year.
How long have you been waiting?
How many times have you called?

examples.en: I've been working as a nurse for twelve years, and for the last four years I've been leading the ICU team.
examples.pt: Trabalho como enfermeira há doze anos, e nos últimos quatro lidero a equipe da UTI.

examples.en: Sorry I'm sweaty — I've been cycling.
What have you been up to lately? — I've been learning to code!
examples.pt: O que você tem feito? — Tenho aprendido a programar!

grammar.tip_pt: **"What have you been up to?"** é uma das perguntas mais comuns ao reencontrar alguém. Responda com present perfect continuous: "I've been working a lot / traveling / taking a course..."

common_mistakes.why_pt: Desde/há + continua = present perfect (continuous), não present continuous.

common_mistakes.wrong: I've been knowing him for years.
I've been drinking five coffees today.
common_mistakes.right: I've drunk / I've had five coffees today.

pronunciation.tip_pt: **I've been** é dito como uma palavra: "áivbin" (americano) ou "áivbín" (britânico). **She's been** = "shízbin". A força vai no verbo principal: "I've been **WORK**ing here for **SIX** years."
practice: I've been working here for six years.

dialogue.title: Job interview
dialogue.context_pt: Fernanda faz uma entrevista online para uma vaga de gerente de projetos numa empresa canadense.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.en: Thanks for joining us, Fernanda. So, tell me about yourself.
lines.pt: Obrigado por participar, Fernanda. Então, fale sobre você.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.en: Sure. I'm a civil engineer, and I've been working in project management for eight years. I started my career at a construction company in São Paulo.
lines.pt: Claro. Sou engenheira civil e trabalho com gestão de projetos há oito anos. Comecei a carreira numa construtora em São Paulo.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.en: And what are you doing now?
lines.pt: E o que você faz atualmente?

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.en: For the last three years, I've been leading a team of twelve at a solar energy company. We've delivered more than forty projects so far.
lines.pt: Nos últimos três anos, lidero uma equipe de doze pessoas numa empresa de energia solar. Já entregamos mais de quarenta projetos até agora.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.en: Impressive. What's your biggest achievement?
lines.pt: Impressionante. Qual é sua maior conquista?

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.en: Last year, I managed our largest project — a solar farm in Bahia. We finished it two months early and under budget.
lines.pt: No ano passado, gerenciei nosso maior projeto — uma usina solar na Bahia. Terminamos dois meses antes e abaixo do orçamento.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.en: And why are you interested in this position?
lines.pt: E por que você se interessa por esta vaga?

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.en: I've been following your company's work in renewable energy for a while, and I'm looking for international challenges. I've also been taking an advanced English course to prepare.
lines.pt: Acompanho o trabalho da empresa em energia renovável há um tempo e estou buscando desafios internacionais. Também tenho feito um curso avançado de inglês para me preparar.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: Hey, Tom! Well, I've been freelancing for about two years now. I've been working mainly with startups.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Nice. Do you like it?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: Love it. I've had clients from five countries so far. And I've been learning Spanish because I've got a big client in Mexico.

lines.en: That's great. Me? Same company, but I've been promoted twice. And I've been running marathons — I've done three this year!

reading.title: The career-change generation
reading.text: For our parents, a career was often a single straight line: one company, one profession, a gold watch at retirement. Today, it looks more like a zigzag. Surveys suggest that many young professionals expect to change careers — not just jobs — several times in their lives. Take Rodrigo, 38. He worked as a lawyer for ten years, but he'd been feeling unhappy for a long time. Three years ago, he started a coding bootcamp at night. "I've been working as a software developer for two years now, and I've never been happier," he says. Experts say the key skills for this new world are adaptability and continuous learning. In other words, the question is no longer "What do you want to be when you grow up?" but "What have you been learning lately?"

culture_note.title: Currículo americano x brasileiro
culture_note.text_pt: Currículos em inglês (**résumé** nos EUA, **CV** no Reino Unido) geralmente **não** têm foto, idade, estado civil, CPF ou endereço completo — isso evita discriminação. O foco é em **conquistas mensuráveis** com verbos de ação: "**Increased** sales by 30%", "**Led** a team of 12", "**Reduced** costs by 15%".
